paragraphs.text: Supermarkets in wealthy countries throw away vast quantities of food that is still safe to eat, often because it has passed a 'best before' date or looks imperfect.
In 2016, France became the first country to ban large supermarkets from destroying unsold food. Instead, they must donate it to charities or use it for animal feed.
Households, however, are responsible for more waste than shops. In the UK, about 70% of food waste after the farm comes from homes, largely because people buy more than they need.
Apps that connect consumers with restaurants selling surplus meals at a discount have become popular, saving millions of meals a year in Europe alone.
